 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act seeking compensation for the injuries and damages caused to motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-KM-0665 Arun Kumar Singh vs Shashank on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23945474/
1 in the road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 22.12.2022 at about 10.00 p.m, when the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-KM-0665 in slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules, when he reached near Ganesha Temple, Mysore Road, Bengaluru City,
at that time the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MS-6595 driven in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the rear side of the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.
Due to the impact he fell down from the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries and the petitioner's motorcycle was extensively SCCH-23 damaged.
After the accident he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He had spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses and he has also spent amount towards repair of motorcycle.
He stated that due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become permanently disabled.
It is further urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel, he failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.

Further the SCCH-23 respondent has contended that the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 134(c) and 158(6)
of M.V.Act.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle / petitioner who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.

On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured,
the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

SCCH-23 5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries and the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05- Arun Kumar Singh vs Shashank on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23945474/
2 KM-0665 sustained damages in a road traffic accident that occurred on 22.12.2022 at about 10.00 p.m, near Ganesha Temple, Mysore Road, Bengaluru City due to actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MS-6595?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 9 were marked on his behalf.
The respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence on their behalf.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
SCCH-23 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.7 lakhs together.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MS-6595 for the offences punishable under section's 279, 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of car.

Therefore, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 'In the Affirmative'.
10. ISSUE NO.2 :

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries :
Swelling and SCCH-23 tenderness over right foot.
The doctor opined that the injury is grievous in nature.
Further the petitioner has not produced the discharge summary.
The documents available on record ie., medical prescriptions of KIMS Hospital and Jayanagar Orthopedi centre, which discloses that he took treatment as an out patient on different dates.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
11. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD :

The petitioner has deposed that he was doing independent business of Mobile shop and was earning Rs.20,000/- to Rs.30,000/- p.m, and due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.

In order to prove the said fact he has not produced any documents Arun Kumar Singh vs Shashank on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23945474/
3 before this Court.

sentences.text: However he has neither proved his avocation nor his earning capacity.
However he has neither examined the doctor nor produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact he has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability.

Though PW.1 SCCH-23 deposed in his evidence affidavit that due to the injuries sustained in the accident he was unable to continue avocation and thereby he sustained loss of income from this accident.
So also no iota of evidence is placed on record to show that he has sustained loss of income during treatment period.
Non- production of the any documents in this regard results in drawing of an inference that he has not suffered any financial loss during the period of his treatment.

Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
12. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :

No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the petitioner has treated as inpatient, except producing wound certificate he has not produced any discharge summary to show that incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.
SCCH-23 13.
PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
14. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
In the chief examination he has not got marked the medical bills.
Further on perusal of documents available on record, 10-Medical bills are found, and he has spent Rs.10,028/- towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross- examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.10,000/- towards medical expenses.
15. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.
16. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further SCCH-23 treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.
17. EXPENSES INCURRED TOWARDS DAMAGES CAUSED TO THE VEHICLE: PW.1 has deposed that in the accident his motorcycle was badly damaged and he has spent substantial amount towards its repair.
In order to substantiate this aspect 3 Tax invoices are exhibited at Ex.P9.
At the outset as per the very admission of PW.1, the motorcycle was owned by his younger brother.
He has also not produced RC to show the ownership.

Hence it is clear that he is not the RC owner of the two wheeler Arun Kumar Singh vs Shashank on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23945474/
4 which was involved in the accident i.e., in respect of which damages are claimed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Furthermore during his cross examination PW.1 stated that the said vehicle was insured by ICICI Lambord and he don't know if a claim has been made against their vehicle by the said company or not.
Further he stated that he has no information whether ICICI Lambord has made the OD claim.
Meaning thereby the said vehicle is insured.
First of SCCH-23 all, Ex.P9 are the tax invoices and they are not the original bills for incurring the amount towards repair of the motorcycle.
Further Ex.P9 are issued after lapse of 2 months from the date accident.
Further more in the said invoices it is clearly mentioned the party : ICICI Lombard Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd.,
Hence it is clear that the said repair cost has been reimbursed from his own insurance company on OD.
Further either the author of Ex.P9 nor the mechanic who repaired the vehicle is examined.
Survey report is not produced.
However no documents are produced to show that he has not received any compensation from the Insurance company of his two wheeler.
In this view of the matter, this Tribunal holds that petitioner is not entitled to any amount under this head.

18. The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Loss of future income due to : - Nil - disability 2 Loss of income during laid-up : -
Nil - period 3
Attendant charges, extra nutritious : - Nil - food & conveyance charges 4 Pain & sufferings : 50,000-00 SCCH-23 5
Medical expenses : 10,000-00 6 Loss of future amenities & : 40,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : - Nil - 8 Expenses incurred towards : - Nil - damages caused to the vehicle Total 1,00,000-00 19.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
20. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MS-6595 thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
SCCH-23 21. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
